scope: Bounded exact checks of route obstructions and a conditional counting lemma; no unrestricted asymptotic advance or novelty assertion.

volume_obstruction.scope: Exact determinant controls for an infinite symbolic construction; the uniform proof is in the research note.
volume_obstruction.conclusion: The full moment-polytope volume has order n^(2d) even in the generic point-ideal case. A smaller universal full-volume bound cannot improve the existing proof.

disjoint_socle_relation_control.uniform_conclusion: For this whole three-variable construction, g(I)=O(n^(4/3)); it cannot beat the existing generic n^2(log n)^2 order.
disjoint_socle_relation_control.proof_location: docs/interleaving_research.md, First feasibility pass: two rigorous route obstructions

overlapping_socle_relations.uniform_conclusion: Arbitrary relation spaces confined to the socle give O_d(n^(d(d-1)/(d+1))) initial staircases, by an antichain coordinate budget and the established lattice-polytope bound.
overlapping_socle_relations.scope_exclusion: Relations with surviving nonconstant multiples are not covered.

rectangular_spanning_control.conditional_conclusion: If every monomial box of volume at least kappa*n spans, every standard basis is determined by a geometric word of length d^d*kappa*n. The existing ordered-prefix theorem then gives O_d((kappa*n)^(d-1)(log(kappa*n+1))^(d-1)).
rectangular_spanning_control.scope_exclusion: The spanning parameter is not universally bounded; the diagonal family has growing parameter and only d initial ideals.

binomial_parallel_class_control.uniform_conclusion: For every colength-n binomial ideal in fixed dimension d>=2, g(I)=O_d(n^(d-1)(log(n+1))^((d-1)^2)), by the known normal-form reduction, hyperbolic cross and Minkowski-sum vertex bound.
binomial_parallel_class_control.priority: Recorded as a consequence of existing tools, not an established novel theorem or an unrestricted advance.

nonpartition_point_control.conclusion: Five distinct nonzero residue lines have rank four. Selecting one representative from each line does not give a basis. The binomial proof does not apply to all point ideals.
nonpartition_point_control.scope: This refutes only the proposed automatic partition-matroid extension, not every possible Minkowski decomposition.

truncated_partition_point_control.rank_rule: Over positive real samples, columns of distinct t-degrees form a generalized Vandermonde matrix; rank equals min(n, number of distinct degrees). This is a truncation of the degree-class partition matroid.
truncated_partition_point_control.scope: A finite realizable test of a proposed lower-family mechanism, not an asymptotic advance or a novelty claim.

pure_power_sector_control.uniform_conclusion: Primitive pure-power relations supply d sector boxes. The lattice-polytope moment bound gives O_A(n^(d-1)) for every finite quotient on a fixed monomial curve, over every field; this rules out a fixed-curve asymptotic separation from the generic order.
pure_power_sector_control.scope: A restricted consequence of the established state-polytope vertex estimate; not an unrestricted improvement or an established novelty claim.

coarse_class_path_control.conclusion: The two different initial staircases are in one connected halfspace-deformation class with the same selected degree classes. A coarse colored k-set count cannot be used directly as the number of initial ideals.

normal_curve_lower_control.uniform_conclusion: The ideals of n distinct positive samples (t,t^2,...,t^d) have Theta_d(n^(d-1)) initial ideals. The full proof combines the fixed-curve upper bound with an explicit open family of ray allocations.
normal_curve_lower_control.scope: A sharp restricted-family control below the existing generic logarithmic order. It does not improve the unrestricted lower bound and novelty has not been established.
normal_curve_lower_control.point_description: For each fixture take t=1,...,n over Q; ray residue i has monomials x_i*x_d^k, with x_0=1.

independent_modular_rank_check.meaning: The integer positive-point evaluation minor is nonzero modulo a proved prime, so it is also nonzero over Q. No uniform finite-field assertion is made.

relative_socle_control.uniform_conclusion: For the stated finite monomial reference (or the justified product reference), relations supported on the relative socle in s specified variables and closed under the remaining multiplications give O_d(n^((2*d-s)*(d-1)/(d+1))) initial ideals. In dimension three the layer argument improves s=1 to O(n^(7/3)); s=2 gives O(n^2), with a matching family of lengths 6L.
relative_socle_control.scope: A restricted mechanism with genuinely surviving z multiples; it cannot beat the existing unrestricted generic lower order. No novelty or unrestricted improvement is asserted.

hook_first_order_deformation_control.uniform_conclusion: Every flat first-order deformation of (y^r,y*z,z^s), r,s>=2, has O((r+s)^2) initial ideals as a length-2(r+s-1) algebra in three variables. Three connecting columns suffice after deleting a coloop and two blocks with O(r+s) internal comparison hyperplanes.
hook_first_order_deformation_control.scope: A proved obstruction for this sparse first-order family, not an unrestricted advance or established novelty claim.

sparse_growing_corner_deformation_contro.uniform_conclusion: Every flat first-order deformation of the sparse plane ideal (y^r,y^k*z,y^(k-1)*z^2,...,y*z^k,z^s), k>=2 and r,s>=2k+1, has O(n^2) initial ideals at quotient length n=2*(r+s-1+k*(k-1)/2). Three residue blocks have total interface dimension at most twelve and a linear number of internal comparison hyperplanes.
sparse_growing_corner_deformation_contro.scope: A uniform growing-corner obstruction, not an unrestricted advance or established novelty claim. These fixtures check exact selected weights and do not enumerate the full fan.

thick_hook_deformation_control.uniform_conclusion: For all compatible thick-hook first-order tails, q<=12*a*b and at most 120*m internal hyperplanes give O(n^2*(a*b)^4) initial ideals by optional-column refinement. Together with the prior annihilator bound this is O(min(n^(7/3),n^2*(a*b)^4)). Fixed thickness is therefore insufficient for a stronger unrestricted lower bound.
thick_hook_deformation_control.scope: A parameter-sensitive restricted upper bound, not an unrestricted advance or novelty claim. These are selected-weight controls, not fan enumeration.

power_substitution_negative_control.scope: Exact selected-weight controls support the uniform free-extension proof; this does not enumerate either full fan.

koszul_support_matching_negative_control.uniform_constraint: For any coefficients, the shifted columns of two polynomials satisfy G*F-F*G=0 whenever these products fit without truncation. The displayed integer specialization has rank exactly five.
koszul_support_matching_negative_control.scope: A classical Koszul relation used as a realizability control, not a novel syzygy theorem or an asymptotic lower bound.

untruncated_convolution_rank_and_basis_c.uniform_conclusion: For coprime nonzero F,G and convex lattice-complete multiplier domains, the kernel is (H*G,-H*F) with H in the Newton-polytope erosion domain. Its translated leading terms determine every coherent basis, and the projected basis polytope is a translate of minus the kernel dimension times the tagged Newton polytope. Common factors may be removed before applying the formula. No quotient truncation is allowed.
untruncated_convolution_rank_and_basis_c.priority: An elementary consequence of the classical two-generator syzygy and Newton-product identity; novelty is not established.

factorial_boundary_control.uniform_conclusion: For I_L=(x^2,z^L-x*A_L(z)) over characteristic zero or p>L-1, length is 2L and there are exactly L+1 global initial ideals, versus two positive coherent bases in the corresponding untruncated convolution. Two disjoint arms give length 4t+2 and exactly (t+1)^2 initial ideals; their interaction dimension is zero.
factorial_boundary_control.scope: A proved boundary mechanism and sharp restricted quadratic control below the existing generic lower order. Classical Toeplitz/Padé ingredients; novelty and an unrestricted advance are not established.

positive_curve_collision_control.uniform_conclusion: Positive monomial-curve divisors of the same length and exponent tuple have identical monomial residue matroids and identical positive Groebner fans, including all collisions with multiplicity. Collision within this class cannot amplify the fan.
positive_curve_collision_control.priority: A consequence of classical sparse positive-root bounds and confluent generalized Vandermonde theory; no new interpolation theorem is claimed.

checks.scope: Finite checks use all seven-box staircases and all 37 saved coherent bases. Equality for every positive divisor of degree n is proved in the note, not inferred from these four profiles.

monogenic_embedding_control.uniform_conclusion: Over characteristic zero, a finite algebra admits an embedding with the labeled generic corner-cut fan if and only if it is monogenic. For every monogenic algebra a nonempty Zariski open set of coordinate tuples has this fan. The fixed abstract curvilinear algebra K[u]/(u^n) has both one-initial-ideal and C_d(n)-initial-ideal embeddings.
monogenic_embedding_control.scope: Generic embeddings are not asserted to maximize the fan count; the existing seven-point countercontrol rules that out. This does not improve G_d or F_d and does not complete the goal.

checks.field_scope: Uniform statements are over characteristic zero; the characteristic-two failure is deliberate.
checks.scope: Classical Vandermonde and open-minor consequences, not a new unrestricted counting theorem or an established novelty claim.

sparse_prefix_interpolation_control.scope: Two-generator module columns inside the actual monomial quotient K[y,z]/(y^R,y^k*z^k,z^R). The full monomial configuration of a three-variable ideal has extra powers of the tag variable and is not counted here.
sparse_prefix_interpolation_control.conclusion: Perfect support matching does not imply normal geometric-prefix rank. This subcheck certifies a nonzero null vector for every fixture and exact rank at k=2. The subsequent graded-Jordan argument determines the uniform exact defect k^2/4.

jordan_filtered_convolution_control.uniform_rank_formula: For distinct scalar nodes tau_i and total-degree cuts a_i, rank of sum_i exp(tau_i*L)*B_{<a_i} is sum_strings min(length,sum_i clamp(a_i-start,0,length)).
jordan_filtered_convolution_control.sparse_family_exact_defect: For every even k>=2 the selected 4k^2-column prefix has rank 4k^2-k^2/4. This follows from the known two-variable strong Lefschetz theorem and the rank formula.
jordan_filtered_convolution_control.scope: This controls total-degree filtrations and the full exponential-graph algebra on diagonal weights. It does not count its full positive Groebner fan or improve the unrestricted asymptotic bounds.

unequal_weight_jordan_countercontrol.conclusion: Even the same graded algebra and the same L and tag element have different full fans under different degree-one generating coordinates. Graded Jordan data determine the proved diagonal support function but not unequal-weight costs or the full fan count.
unequal_weight_jordan_countercontrol.scope: Exact falsification certificates for a transfer lemma, not an asymptotic lower bound or a novelty claim.

codimension_one_binomial_quotient_contro.uniform_scope: Every ideal I containing a colength-q binomial ideal J, with dim(I/J)=1, over every field, in dimensions two and three.
codimension_one_binomial_quotient_contro.count_bound: O(M*alpha(M)) in dimension two and O(M^2*alpha(M)) in dimension three, M=|V_q^d|. Thus O(q^2*log(q+1)^4*alpha(q*(1+log(q))^2)) in dimension three.
codimension_one_binomial_quotient_contro.geometric_input: Pach--Sharir (1989), Theorem 1-prime, the segment-envelope bound and the overlay argument of Lemma 2.2.
codimension_one_binomial_quotient_contro.decision: Deleting one point from a cyclic binomial orbit cannot produce an n^(2+epsilon) lower family in three variables for fixed epsilon>0. The unrestricted goal is not completed; logarithmic improvements are not ruled out.
codimension_one_binomial_quotient_contro.priority: A consequence of established binomial normal forms and envelope bounds; novelty has not been established.

uniform_deletion_and_dual_relation_contr.uniform_geometric_bound: For q nonempty parallel classes on M points and rank n=q-r uniform truncation, the number of positive coherent bases is O(M*(r+1)*alpha(M)) in dimension two and O(M^2*(r+1)*alpha(M)) in dimension three.
uniform_deletion_and_dual_relation_contr.algebraic_specialization: Prime cyclic orbit subsets over C, and consecutive samples for any cyclic orbit size. With M<=q*(1+log(q))^2, the spatial bound is O(q^2*(r+1)*(1+log(q))^4*alpha(q*(1+log(q))^2)).
uniform_deletion_and_dual_relation_contr.cyclotomic_certificate_scope: A nonzero product of the indicated Fourier minors after reduction certifies their simultaneous nonvanishing over C. No implication from complex nonvanishing to all finite characteristics is used.

nonuniform_two_relation_countercontrol.kernel_description: The six-root orbit with t=1 and t=-1 removed; (x,y,z)=(t,t^2,t^3).
nonuniform_two_relation_countercontrol.conclusion: A general quotient of a binomial algebra requires dual-matroid basis optimization. The uniform truncation rule and level bound cannot be asserted for it without a separate hypothesis.

uniform_deletion_and_dual_relation_contr.priority: Uses established envelope bounds, elementary random-sampling estimates and standard matroid duality. Novelty and an unrestricted asymptotic advance are not established.

attention_exact_rank_sanity_control.logit_formula: S_ij=i*log(t_j), a rank-one outer product; d=1, with i=0,1,2,3.
attention_exact_rank_sanity_control.scope: For all sequence lengths, distinct positive t_j give a full-rank Vandermonde attention matrix despite rank-at-most-one logits (rank one when N>=2). This classical observation does not rule out accurate approximate low-rank computation or establish novelty.

box_residual_duality_control.uniform_statement: For every J contained in I, on every term-order cone where in(J)=(x_1^s_1,...,x_d^s_d), in(J:I)=in(J):in(I), with reflected complementary box standard bases. This holds over every field without radicality or comaximality.
box_residual_duality_control.grid_consequence: Every univariate grid parent has the same box at all global orders, so I and J:I have identical positive initial-ideal fans and complementary lengths.
box_residual_duality_control.scope_limit: A complete-intersection parent alone is insufficient: its initial ideal must be a box for this invertible recovery. General grid covers can have residual length n^d-n and do not improve the unrestricted bound.

nonbox_countercontrol.information_loss: Both colons are identical, but coloning again adds both parent socle monomials rather than recovering either of the two different child initials.

box_residual_duality_control.priority: Standard complete-intersection duality plus the initial-colon inclusion; the grid-complement fan correspondence is established prior art. No new unrestricted theorem or novelty certification.

nonuniform_two_level_exchange_control.parent_definition: The monomial complement of the union of the divisor boxes of the six displayed socle corners.
nonuniform_two_level_exchange_control.conclusion: Nonuniform rank-two relation matroids can have independent simultaneous exchanges at different costs. The single-cutoff vertex argument for uniform truncations does not extend to arbitrary quotient matroids.
nonuniform_two_level_exchange_control.limit: The example is supported on the full socle, so the already proved O(n^(3/2)) support-class bound applies. It is not an exponent-amplifying family. Nonuniform fixed defect outside that class is not excluded by the uniform-defect theorem.

nonuniform_grid_deletion_control.uniform_scope: Every even v>=4 and every positive multiple u of v with u>=v, over every field: J=(xz-y,y^u-1,z^v-1), I=J+(sum_{a=0}^{u-1} sum_{0<=b<v, b even} y^a*z^b).
nonuniform_grid_deletion_control.length_and_upper_bound: The child has n=uv-2 and g(I)<=18*v^2+34*v+2=O(n). In characteristic zero it removes the two points (1,1,1),(-1,1,-1) from the full torus grid graph.
nonuniform_grid_deletion_control.nonannihilation: On the two-dimensional relation ideal, y acts as identity and x,z swap its displayed basis. These actions are invertible, so this is outside the variable-annihilated full-socle construction.
nonuniform_grid_deletion_control.unbounded_initial_socle_type: At weights (u+1,u,u), the parent initial algebra has 2*v-1 socle monomials. The count bound does not assume bounded initial type.
nonuniform_grid_deletion_control.decision: Independent exchanges persist outside socle-supported constructions, but the whole divisible-grid family has only linear growth and cannot provide the required n^(2+epsilon) lower family. No unrestricted upper advance or novelty certification.

coordinate_moment_range_control.scope: Every finite-colength ideal over every field, using any univariate grid cover. The n-based consequence uses its minimal coordinate elimination degrees.
coordinate_moment_range_control.uniform_bound: g(I)<=C_d*(product_i (W_i+1))^((d-1)/(d+1)), with W_i the exact coordinate-moment width of n-element downsets in its grid box.
coordinate_moment_range_control.worst_case_limit: Minimal degrees s_i<=n recover the old unrestricted exponent. No qualifying worst-case asymptotic improvement or novelty is asserted.

grading_and_perturbation_control.graded_scope: Any multigraded finite quotient over every field has all monomial-basis moments on the grading affine subspace. The dimension-sensitive count uses the established relative-lattice vertex estimate.
grading_and_perturbation_control.uniform_bound: If h independent integer gradings make I homogeneous and r=d-h, then g(I)<=1 for r=0, <=2 for r=1, and O_d(n^(2*r*(r-1)/(r+1))) for r>=2.
grading_and_perturbation_control.perturbation_scope: Over Q, for each n>=3, a finite excluded set of epsilon values contains every possible staircase determinant zero. Epsilon=0 has three initials, whereas sufficiently small nonzero epsilon has C_3(n). The same fixed abstract algebra and all three elimination degrees n persist.
grading_and_perturbation_control.priority: Consequences of established multigrading, lattice-polytope and open-minor arguments, not a new unrestricted asymptotic theorem or certified novelty.

minimum_product_rank_control.scope: Uniform proof covers every field, n>=3, all cyclic-coordinate algebras satisfying the minimum bilinear ranks, including nonreduced quotients. One unsaturated minimum-growth box with every side at least two forces this class. Bounded fixtures test reduced and nilpotent presentations.
minimum_product_rank_control.uniform_count: If the d fractional-linear coordinates have pole-group sizes m_j, then g(I)=[z^(n-1)] product_j(1+m_j*z/(1-z)).
minimum_product_rank_control.uniform_box_rank: Every anchored monomial box of side lengths a_i has rank min(n,1+sum_i(a_i-1)); every proper box span has scalar stabilizer in the algebra.
minimum_product_rank_control.information_loss: The same complete box-rank profile and stabilizer dimensions allow g=d or g=binom(n+d-2,d-1). Three-monomial flags retain pole information lost by box ranks.
minimum_product_rank_control.priority: Uses elementary cyclic multiplication, fractional-linear algebra and partial fractions. The coding Kneser theorem and critical-pair theory are prior art. No unrestricted asymptotic improvement or publication novelty is asserted.

product_excess_and_extension_control.scope: All-field structural proofs are in the note. Reconstruction uses cyclic coordinates and 2*b-2<n. Extension counting requires coordinate-compatible containment and a bound on all smaller initial-ideal generator counts.
product_excess_and_extension_control.rank_tradeoff: For the nonzero two-by-b relation kernel, rank=b+rational_degree+exceptional_ideal_dimension; these last two quantities sum to at most excess+1 for a larger near-minimum unsaturated rectangle.
product_excess_and_extension_control.extension_bound: If I is contained in J, lengths differ by e and every initial ideal of J has at most q minimal generators, then g(I)<=g(J)*product_(j=0)^(e-1)(q+(d-1)*j).
product_excess_and_extension_control.priority: Rational reconstruction, relation modules and minimal monomial generators are established tools. These consequences do not prove a new unrestricted asymptotic bound or certified publication novelty.

quadratic_pole_flag_control.uniform_conclusion: For every field and every fixed d>=3, all length-n finite quotients with coordinates t,t^(-2),(t-lambda_3)^(-1),...,(t-lambda_d)^(-1), at distinct nonzero poles avoiding the divisor, have O_d(n^(d-1)*log(n+1)) monomial initial ideals. For d=2 the bound is O(n).
quadratic_pole_flag_control.scope: The proof uses minimum admissible parity gaps and is uniform in the divisor, poles and characteristic. It remains restricted and does not improve the unrestricted asymptotic bound.
quadratic_pole_flag_control.encoding: A pattern table key is (n,d,chosen_axis). Each row is (a,b0,b1,other_axis_chain_lengths), with other axes increasing and excluding y and the chosen axis; QP2 reconstructs the exact basis. Border normals and polygon vertices are comma-separated exact coordinate strings.

staircase_moment_cube_control.uniform_cube: For every fixed d>=2 and all sufficiently large n, moments of actual n-element downsets contain a translated 3*[0,R^2]^d integer grid, with R=Theta_d(n). Four disjoint (1,-2,1) row patches, Lagrange's theorem and fixed-row padding prove this.
staircase_moment_cube_control.relaxation_extremal_order: The maximum positive exposed-moment count of an arbitrary family of n-element staircases is Theta_d(n^(2*d*(d-1)/(d+1))). The lower bound uses the classical Barany--Larman integer-ball theorem; the upper uses the existing lattice-polytope bound.
staircase_moment_cube_control.scope: A sharp obstruction to improving the unrestricted bound using only individual downsets and their moments. No common quotient, representable residue matroid or improved G_d/F_d bound is supplied.
staircase_moment_cube_control.row_encoding: Rows j=0,...,12 contain x=0,...,ell_j-1. Cyclic arm i uses coordinates i and (i+1) mod d. Padding extends the first pure axis from B=50*R+25 by the stated count.

integer_ball_relaxation_checks.scope: Exposed only within this explicit family of staircases; not certified initial ideals of a common algebra.

algebraic_attention_hotpath_control.scope: Exact reference computation for deliberately constrained polynomial query/key embeddings, an instance of established polynomial-kernel compression. No new ML algorithm, GPU speedup or quality equivalence is asserted.
algebraic_attention_hotpath_control.identity: For A={0,...,m}^s minus {0}, S(q,k)=sum_(a in A) theta_a*q^a*k^a and p2(S)=1+S+S^2/2 have support B={0,...,2m}^s. Positive theta give a diagonal separable representation with |B| features.
algebraic_attention_hotpath_control.cost: With s fixed, D=(m+1)^s-1, M=(2m+1)^s, value width v and T tokens: O(T*M*(s+v+1)) arithmetic, O(M*(v+1)) streaming state, plus latent-encoder costs. Direct coefficient setup is O(D^2*s), outside the token loop but charged whenever weights change. This is a forward streaming bound, not constant-memory training.
limits: The latent embedding and tied polynomial coefficients restrict the interaction class; arbitrary Q/K or dense learned mixing do not retain the diagonal collapse.
The kernel is quadratic Taylor attention, not exact exponential softmax. Exact rational checks do not establish floating-point conditioning or trainability.
The algebraic reduction is existing kernel-on-variety methodology; scientific novelty requires a stronger comparison and an additional theorem or useful measured model advantage.

algebraic_attention_mixing_control.scope: Elementary polynomial collection with arbitrary bilinear mixing and a classical Vandermonde state-rank witness; no new ML method, benchmark, unrestricted Q/K compression or trained-quality claim.
algebraic_attention_mixing_control.identity: S(q,k)=sum H[a,b]*q^a*k^b gives p2(S)=u(q)^T*C*u(k) on the doubled exponent box, even for dense nonsymmetric H. The coefficient matrix C is generally dense.
algebraic_attention_mixing_control.cost: M*(v+1) recurrent state, O(M*v) update/read plus O(M^2) query transformation and O(M^2) coefficient storage; naive coefficient preparation O(D^4*s), charged when H changes. Encoders and training/backward cost are additional.
algebraic_attention_mixing_control.rank_limit: For distinct real t_j, Z[r,c]=sum_j t_j^(r+c)=V*V^T has rank min(N,L) in an L-by-L moment state. Rank-one token updates therefore do not imply a fixed-rank state under accumulation.

algebraic_power_delta_control.scope: Exact reference for a constrained normalized even-power feature map and ordinary scalar-gated delta recurrence. Existing kernel-on-variety and DeltaNet methodology; no novelty, hardware or trained-quality claim.
algebraic_power_delta_control.restriction: Shared positive feature weights are constant across one sequence; query/key embeddings lie on the specified monomial variety. Arbitrary coordinate-wise gates or mixing need not preserve the subspace.

algebraic_channel_gate_control.scope: Elementary invariant-subspace closure for an explicitly constrained KDA-style architecture. No new general attention method, trained-quality advantage or GPU speedup is asserted.
algebraic_channel_gate_control.criterion: For U^T U=I, a linear gate A preserves the compressed state exactly iff (I-U U^T) A U=0. For diagonal generic gates and positive grouping weights, this holds iff the gate is constant within each equal-exponent group.
algebraic_channel_gate_control.architecture: Use any independently learned gate per collected exponent, then the ordinary KDA delta correction. This retains arbitrary collected-channel forgetting at M*v state and O(M*v) recurrent arithmetic, plus all feature, encoder and gate costs.

algebraic_erase_write_control.scope: Exact algebraic compatibility with the published Gated DeltaNet-2 update, not a new recurrence, trained-model result or performance benchmark.
algebraic_erase_write_control.criterion: For f=U*phi and U^T*U=I, tied group decay preserves im(U); arbitrary generic erase gates reduce to U^T*diag(b)*U, a diagonal weighted group average. Value-axis write gates are unrestricted.
algebraic_erase_write_control.cost_caveat: M-row recurrence costs O(M*v), but computing generic F-row erase gates and averaging still costs at least O(F). Generate M-row gates directly for an economical architecture; this does not preserve arbitrary nonlinear gate-encoder parameterizations.

lattice_shadow_control.scope: Exact finite supporting certificates for the uniform proof in the note; they do not numerically integrate random shadows, prove isoperimetry, establish novelty or replace the dimension-uniform argument.

polytope_fixtures.name: generic rational point quotient basis polytope

lattice_shadow_sharpness_control.scope: Primitive zonotopes are an established family. The note supplies a uniform proof that their growth saturates the proposed lattice surface/shadow inequality; these finite controls do not establish novelty, the asymptotics or quotient realizability.
lattice_shadow_sharpness_control.uniform_growth: For fixed d>=3 and primitive generators up to sign in [-p,p]^d: f0=Theta_d(p^(d*(d-1))), S=Theta_d(p^(d*d-1)), and mean shadow=Theta_d(p^d).
lattice_shadow_sharpness_control.limitation: Neither geometric exponent can be reduced with the other held fixed in a uniform pure-power bound. This does not prove sharpness of G_d or of the looser Dey-based matroid specialization.

axis_box_controls.scope: Small density controls, below the sufficient asymptotic threshold; no finite threshold inference.
Small density controls, below the sufficient asymptotic threshold; no finite threshold inference.

bounded_grid_shadow_control.scope: Uniform cover-sensitive consequence of the lattice-shadow bound and established grid residual duality, over every field including nonreduced separated parents. The original unrestricted objective is retained; no new duality or numerical finite-size dominance is asserted.
bounded_grid_shadow_control.parameters: Q=product b_i, h=min(n,Q-n)>0, p_i=min(b_i-1,h-1), M=#{u:0<=u_i<b_i,product(u_i+1)<=h}, A=sum_i product_(j!=i)(h*p_j+1).
bounded_grid_shadow_control.generator_consequence: Each reduced basis has at most Q-n+d elements, as well as the classical O_d(n^((d-1)/d)) bound. Multiply the smaller generator budget by the count bound for the union.

staircase_generator_control.scope: Finite supporting certificates for the established minimal-generator estimate used in the universal-basis corollary. No new generator theorem or uniform proof by enumeration is claimed.
staircase_generator_control.method: Enumerate small staircases; compare one-step minimal borders against independent coordinate-fiber caps, and certify the disjoint-chain packing bound exactly.

exchange_cycle_coherence_control.general_lemma: For a common basis D and two-for-two competing bases, contract the common n-2 entries. A new monomial u-alpha*e_i+beta*e_j replaces at least one of u,u+h*e_i. A directed coordinate cycle with product(alpha)>product(beta) therefore forces a convex combination of actual bases whose moment is strictly below mu(D) on every cycle coordinate. D cannot be initial under any global monomial order.
exchange_cycle_coherence_control.scope: A self-contained use of established basis exchange and state-polyhedron theory. It is a coherence obstruction, not a characterization, unrestricted fan count, or certified novel theorem.
exchange_cycle_coherence_control.uniform_template_consequence: For every R>=2 and any padding delta>=0, if all 33 radius-two-ball-indexed staircases from the prior moment construction are bases of one quotient, none is initial for that quotient. The three axial candidates fail their inward-neighbor ratio condition; the central candidate has a forced average moment at least (4R-2)/3 lower in each coordinate.
exchange_cycle_coherence_control.limits: This closes this small-ball encoding at all weights and all lengths in the family. It does not exclude other encodings, large-ball families, or improve G_d/F_d. The supplied templates are conditional basis comparisons, not a claim of global quotient realization from independent contraction matrices.

rational_cycle_controls.scope: Feasible weak ratios only; no initial-basis existence is asserted.
